transcript:
-- Meeting Header --
Date: 2027-05-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO - Halcyon), Liam O'Neil (Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (Procurement)

-- Auto-generated Summary --
(brief): Renewal and expansion check-in. Discussed dedicated capacity upgrade options, additional regions, contract extension pricing, and security/operational requirements for VPC and KMS. Agreed to run pilot benchmarks and share SOC2 docs.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is maya from redwood, i'll kick off real quick. priya, liam, sofia, good to see you, thanks for making time.
[00:08] Priya: thanks maya, yep excited to chat, we've been looking at the usage numbers and wanna talk renewal and adding more capacity.
[00:15] Diego: hey all, diego here, i'll handle the bench/technical side, happy to run through perf numbers, current cluster config, etc.
[00:22] Liam: quick note, on the calendar we flagged dedicated capacity and also the multi-year pricing.
[00:26] Sofia: and procurement will need security docs, so SOC two and iso and the vpc deployment details.
[00:33] Maya: perfect, that's what we'll cover. quick high level — halcyon is coming up for renewal in August, right? and you're running hosted now with occasional spikes that you want to move to dedicated for predictability?
[00:42] Priya: yeah august 15th is renewal. current run rate is about 12 million tokens a month, peak spikes sometimes double that. latency's fine, but cost and throttling during spikes are what we wanna address.
[00:54] Diego: so two main asks we heard: reserved/dedicated capacity to smooth spikes and add regions to reduce round-trip for EU and APAC. correct?
[01:02] Priya: yep, and ideally a 3-year commitment if the numbers look good — we want to lock price.
[01:07] Maya: okay great, i'll run through the proposed tiers. we can do a small-medium-large reserved pool model; for you given 12m tokens typical and 24m peak, i'd recommend the medium reserved pool with burst capacity enabled. that gets you predictable throughput with 20-30% lower unit cost vs hosted on-demand.
[01:22] Liam: what's the SLA on latency if we go dedicated? our SLOs are 150 ms p50 and 400 ms p95 for chat paths, sometimes we care about seq length that bumps latency.
[01:34] Diego: dedicated gets stronger latency SLOs — the runtime prioritizes low latency tails for pinned customers. the 150/400 targets are achievable with the medium pool in us-east-1; for longer sequences we may see tail increases, but we have kernel selection and quantization profiles to help.
[01:49] Priya: and for EU and APAC, are they separate physical pools? we need data residency in eu-west-1 for some customers.
[01:57] Maya: yes, we can provision dedicated pools in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. you'll be able to route by policy so EU traffic stays in region and we can set routing to fail over to us-east as fallback during outages.
[02:10] Liam: cost impact of adding regions? if we add two extra regions how much will unit cost change?
[02:16] Maya: adding regions adds fixed reserved capacity cost per region; unit token cost per region is similar but total committed spend increases. we can show a blended unit price in the proposal. for a 3-year commit we usually give a 10-18% discount depending on size.
[02:29] Sofia: procurement question — we need SOC2 type two report, iso 27001, and a data processing addendum. can you share those? also SSO, SAML, SCIM for provisioning.
[02:40] Diego: absolutely — we'll attach SOC two and ISO docs. on the VPC side, for Private deployment we provide a customer-managed VPC peering option; we've got KMS integrations for envelope encryption and HSM support for keys if needed.
[02:53] Priya: great. when you say "VPC peering" — is that for the private control plane or the inference plane? for our compliance we need the inference plane traffic to stay on our VPC.
[03:03] Maya: good clarification — with our Private on-prem/VPC option, you can host the inference plane inside your network while control plane remains in Redwood or we can offer a private control plane under enterprise package. diego, correct me if I'm off.
[03:13] Diego: right. inference plane can be in your VPC (customer-managed infra) or we can provision in our dedicated regional pool with private connectivity. both support KMS/HSM. caveat: fully air-gapped on-prem is a separate install with a slightly different pricing profile.
[03:27] Liam: ok that helps. for the pilot, we want to run throughput benchmarks with our test set — particularly conversational flows with 3 session-turns average. diego, you'll run that?
[03:36] Diego: yes, i can provision a pilot cluster sized to mimic the medium reserved pool and run your test corpus. we should expect to see steady throughput improvements and lower per-token latency vs hosted with prefix caching enabled.
[03:48] Priya: couple of things — do you support prefix/K-V cache seeding? our app relies heavily on cached KV entries.
[03:55] Diego: we do support KV cache and prefix caching; the transcription sometimes calls it "K-V cash" in internal notes, haha — but yeah it's supported, and we can seed caches for warm-up runs.
[04:06] Maya: another note on rollouts — if we do the extension, we recommend a canary-first rollout of the larger pool to route a percentage of traffic while we measure cost/latency, then ramp. minimal churn.
[04:17] Sofia: procurement — contract extension length? we're open to 1 or 3 years; 3-year better for discount but procurement needs flexibility on renewals aligned to fiscal years.
[04:26] Maya: we can draft a 3-year term with a 90-day opt-out clause after year one for enterprise terms; legal will draft language. we'll include pricing tiers for 1-year and 3-year options.
[04:37] Priya: what about overage handling during unexpected spikes above committed throughput?
[04:42] Diego: we offer burst capacity credits for sudden spikes; if you exceed burst credits regularly we'd step up to a higher reserved pool. pricing model will show overage rate; it's generally higher than committed unit price.
[04:53] Liam: curious about metrics/observability — how granular are logs? we need per-route latency and token-level cost for our budget owners.
[05:00] Maya: Redwood Console gives per-route / per-model dashboards with token-level cost, traces, sampling of responses, and exportable CSVs. we can increase retention with the observability add-on.
[05:11] Priya: any caveats with model variants? we use a quantized variant in prod for cost reasons. will fallback model variants be compatible across regions?
[05:20] Diego: good question — we maintain compatible model families per region, but some quantization profiles are hardware-dependent. we'll outline recommended quantization profiles per region in the proposal and fallback policies.
[05:32] Sofia: procurement also needs a list of sub-processors and where data is stored.
[05:37] Maya: we'll include the sub-processor list and data residency mapping.
[05:41] Priya: ok, timeline wise — we need final decision by July 20 to align with your August renewal and our budget cycle. is that workable?
[05:49] Maya: yes, that's tight but doable. action plan: we'll send updated pricing and a contract term sheet by June 3, provision pilot cluster for benchmarks the week of June 7, and meet after benchmarks to finalize.
[05:59] Liam: can we do a short technical session just with diego to define the benchmark test harness?
[06:03] Diego: absolutely — i'll send a calendar invite and a short checklist of what i need (test set, expected concurrency, seq lengths).
[06:11] Sofia: procurement note — we'll need any third-party security attestations before legal signs.
[06:15] Maya: understood. i'll compile SOC 2, ISO, DPA, subprocessor list, and vpc guide into a single package.
[06:22] Priya: sounds good, thanks.
[06:24] Maya: quick recap of next steps — maya send proposal + pricing (due 6/3), diego provision pilot + run benchmarks (due 6/8), priya confirm regions (due 6/2), sofia share procurement timeline (due 6/4). we'll reconvene after pilot. any other questions?
[06:39] Priya: none from me.
[06:41] Liam: all good.
[06:42] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[06:43] Maya: thanks team, bye.
